reader.decision: Set BOUNCE_RETRY_LIMIT to 3 and BOUNCE_RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS to 900 now, together with the sender and relay changes. Defer hard/soft bounce detection until hard bounces are shown to be common.
reader.decision_reason: The config change is small, needs no new code, and stops the retry pattern that would get the new sender blocked for 24 hours. The message gives no evidence that hard bounces are common, which is the condition for making detection the primary fix.

reconstruction.problem: With BOUNCE_RETRY_LIMIT=12 and a 60 second interval, one recipient with a full mailbox bounces every minute. The sixth bounce lands at about minute 5. smtp-mx-2 blocks a sender for 24 hours when one recipient bounces more than 5 times in one hour.
reconstruction.what_breaks: smtp-mx-2 blocks invoices@mail.larkspur.io for 24 hours. Every invoice to every customer is refused because of one full mailbox.
reconstruction.fix: In mailer/config.py, set BOUNCE_RETRY_LIMIT to 3 and BOUNCE_RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS to 900. Also set FROM_ADDRESS to invoices@mail.larkspur.io and SMTP_RELAY to smtp-mx-2.larkspur.internal. The alternative is hard/soft bounce detection in mailer/bounces.py, where hard bounces are never retried.
reconstruction.cost: The config change slows delivery to mailboxes that free up quickly. It leaves one bounce of margin, so other mail to the same recipient in the same hour can still trigger the block. The alternative costs new SMTP status parsing code.

reader.closing_answer: Set the limit to 3 and the interval to 900 seconds. Do not build hard/soft bounce detection first. Revisit it if hard bounces turn out to be common. Then give me the cutover date item.
